twelve_factor_compliance.name: Codebase
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Mainframe PDS/Panvalet libraries can be migrated into Git repositories with branching.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Establish unified Git repository with trunk-based development.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Dependencies
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Dynamic CALL statements (0 found) and STEPLIB/JOBLIB concatenate implicit search orders.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Declare external libraries in Maven/Gradle/Go modules or container image manifest.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Config
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Environment parameters, dataset names, and CICS region IDs are hardcoded in JCL cards and COBOL WORKING-STORAGE.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Externalize parameters to Kubernetes ConfigMaps and Secrets injected as environment variables.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Backing Services
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Tightly bound to local mainframe subsystems (VSAM RLS, DB2 Subsystem ID). 3 VSAM datasets bound to physical DASD volumes.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Abstract databases, message queues, and object storage behind standard URIs and connection pools.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Build, Release, Run
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Mainframe compile/link-edit separates binaries from execution, easily adaptable to container multi-stage builds.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Containerize build step using Red Hat Universal Base Image (UBI) and Tekton / OpenShift Pipelines.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Processes
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: 1 conversational CICS programs hold task and terminal memory across user interactions.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Refactor to pseudo-conversational with external Redis/Memcached session stores, or adopt stateless REST.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Port Binding
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: BMS 3270 maps communicate through SNA terminal LU pools rather than self-contained HTTP/gRPC port binding.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Expose HTTP/REST or gRPC endpoints bound to container ports 8080/8443, fronted by OpenShift Routes.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Concurrency
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Mainframe relies on scale-up vertical MIPS and CICS multi-region operation (MRO). Concurrent pod scaling blocked by file locks.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Enable OpenShift Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) using CPU/memory and custom Prometheus metrics.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Disposability
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Mainframe programs expect warm region memory pools; cold startup overhead requires optimization.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Implement Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes with graceful SIGTERM termination hooks.

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Dev/Prod Parity
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Massive disparity between developer workstations (Windows/macOS x86) and production IBM z/OS mainframes.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Standardize on containerized local dev environment (Minikube / OpenShift Local / Podman Desktop).

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Logs
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: Logs directed to spool datasets (SYSOUT, CESE, JESMSGLG) with rigid 132-character record layouts.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Direct structured JSON logs to stdout/stderr; collect via OpenShift Logging (Fluentd / Vector / OpenSearch).

twelve_factor_compliance.name: Admin Processes
twelve_factor_compliance.gap_analysis: JCL batch jobs naturally map to Kubernetes one-off Jobs and CronJobs.
twelve_factor_compliance.remediation: Convert administrative JCL scripts to containerized Kubernetes Jobs executed via oc create job.

risks.title: Stateful Conversational CICS Transactions
risks.description: Programs ['POLC100'] hold internal state and active task locks across terminal interactions.
risks.migration_impact: Fatal blocker for stateless horizontal pod autoscaling on OpenShift (Factor VI: Processes). Session memory is tied to single runtime instances.
risks.remediation_strategy: Refactor into pseudo-conversational architecture using external session stores (Redis) or expose RESTful stateless APIs with JWT tokens.

risks.title: Self-Modifying Code (ALTER Statement)
risks.description: Detected 1 ALTER statements across 1 program(s). ALTER dynamically mutates GO TO targets at runtime.
risks.migration_impact: Cannot run reliably in stateless container runtimes or modern multi-threaded architectures.
risks.remediation_strategy: Mandatory elimination: replace ALTER with standard PERFORM or EVALUATE state machines.

risks.title: VSAM Dataset Dependencies
risks.description: Found 3 VSAM dataset(s). Requires data conversion to relational or document storage.
risks.migration_impact: Containers cannot mount native VSAM datasets directly.
risks.remediation_strategy: Convert VSAM clusters to relational tables using AWS DMS, Qlik, or custom ETL.

risks.title: RACF SURROGAT Identity Impersonation
risks.description: Application relies on RACF SURROGAT class to switch identity contexts without password re-verification.
risks.migration_impact: Must be replaced with OAuth2 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) or mTLS SPIFFE/SPIRE identity attestation on OpenShift.
risks.remediation_strategy: Implement OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange or Kubernetes ServiceAccount impersonation.

risks.title: BMS 3270 Green-Screen User Interface Coupling
risks.description: Portfolio includes 1 BMS mapsets containing 3270 datastreams, cursor positions, and Modified Data Tags (MDT).
risks.migration_impact: Requires terminal emulation middleware or complete front-end UI re-architecture (React/Angular/Vue).
risks.remediation_strategy: Generate OpenAPI REST specifications from BMS field layouts and build modern responsive web components.

risks.title: Generation Data Group (GDG) Versioning Dependencies
risks.description: Detected 2 GDG dataset references across 1 jobs. GDG relative generation references (e.g. (+1), (0)) are specific to z/OS catalog management.
risks.migration_impact: Cloud storage (S3/Ceph) lacks native automated generational rolling rollbacks.
risks.remediation_strategy: Replace GDG rolling with timestamped object prefixes or MinIO/S3 versioned bucket policies.

risks.title: Complex JCL COND Step Branching
risks.description: 1 job(s) utilize conditional return-code branching (e.g., COND=(4,LT)).
risks.migration_impact: Requires translation into Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) in Kubernetes/Argo/Airflow.
risks.remediation_strategy: Refactor step conditionals into Airflow BranchPythonOperator or Argo Workflows 'when' expressions.

assessment.initial_disposition: Replatform (Containerized COBOL / Lift & Reshape on OCP)

decision.recommended_disposition: Replatform (Containerized COBOL / Lift & Reshape on OCP)
decision.decision_summary: RECOMMENDATION: LINUX VIRTUAL MACHINE (VM) REHOST / REPLATFORM (Score: 80.0/100 vs OCP: 53.0/100). The application has 1 container blocker(s) (e.g. 1 conversational CICS program(s) bind terminal state to memory, violating pod statelessness.). Hosting on Linux VMs via an enterprise mainframe emulation runtime achieves fastest time-to-value while eliminating mainframe MIPS, serving as Phase 1 before gradual container refactoring.

logical_justification.summary: 1. ARCHITECTURAL IMPEDANCE MISMATCH: Direct containerization on OpenShift is constrained by 1 critical blocker(s): 1 conversational CICS program(s) bind terminal state to memory, violating pod statelessness.. 2. PRESERVATION OF STATE & CONCURRENCY: Hosting on Linux Virtual Machines running an enterprise mainframe emulator (such as Micro Focus Enterprise Server or AWS Blu Age) provides native support for conversational CICS regions, shared CWA/TWA memory pools, and POSIX record-level VSAM file emulation. 3. RISK MITIGATION & VELOCITY: Rehosting to VMs allows the organization to cut z/OS hardware and MIPS software fees immediately (often saving 60-70% TCO) without incurring the regression risks of a multi-year complete application rewrite. Once stabilized on Linux VMs, modular services can be incrementally extracted into OpenShift containers.

trade_off_matrix.analysis: OCP scales pods in seconds via HPA; VMs require minutes to spin up and load images.
VM rehosting requires minimal code modification; OCP requires refactoring state and batch orchestration.
OCP runs open-source runtimes with standard subscriptions; VMs often require specialized legacy emulation licenses.
VMs support long-lived conversational memory and TWA/CWA; OCP strictly mandates stateless processes.
VMs emulate OS-level shared file systems and record locking; OCP containers require externalized distributed data grids.
Kubernetes/OpenShift attracts modern cloud engineers; legacy VM emulation maintains specialized skills barrier.
VMs bypass container overlay networks (SDN/OVN) and service mesh proxies, saving 2-5ms per hop.
OCP aligns with enterprise cloud-native roadmap; VM rehost is often viewed as technical debt deferral.

3 shared VSAM dataset(s) lack POSIX distributed record-level lock semantics across container replicas.
1 self-modifying ALTER statement(s) prevent thread-safe container execution.

platform_candidates.migration_path: Replatform (Containerized COBOL / Lift & Reshape on OCP) / Lift-and-Shift to Linux VMs
platform_candidates.estimated_cost_index: Low Capital / Medium Operational (Emulation Software Subscriptions)
pros: Full compatibility with stateful CICS conversational programs and shared memory (CWA/TWA).

Lowest code modification risk: allows verbatim compilation of existing COBOL business logic.
